title: Spivak · Calculus on Manifolds — Interaktiv
category_reason: Pure differential-geometric/analytic exposition of Spivak's book (differential forms, Stokes, manifolds) with no AI/ML application; only points forward to de Rham cohomology and gauge-theory physics.
thesis: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Green's theorem, the Divergence theorem and Stokes' theorem are not four theorems but one (int_M dω = int_{∂M} ω) in four disguises; the proof is trivial (Fubini + 1D FTC) while the real work is in the definitions (alternating tensors, wedge, d, chains, ∂, orientation, manifolds, partition of unity).
key_claims: HDI, Green, Divergence and classical Stokes are a single statement ∫ dω = ∫_{∂} ω with different k and different ω; the classical notation (cross products, normal vectors) is just bookkeeping artifacts of ℝ³.
The proof of Stokes is 'a complete triviality' (three lines: Fubini + 1D fundamental theorem); the difficulty is entirely in the definitions — Spivak's own diagnosis from the preface.
The derivative is not a number but a linear map; Spivak's linear-approximation definition lives in every dimension, whereas the school formula fails because h is a vector and you cannot divide by it.
The determinant is the prototype of all differential forms: it is linear in each column and flips sign under column swap — the two properties that define alternating tensors.
d² = 0 (forms) and ∂² = 0 (chains) are the dual structures; Stokes' theorem says d and ∂ are adjoint with respect to the integral.
'Closed ⇒ exact' holds only on star-shaped regions (Poincaré lemma); dθ on ℝ²∖{0} is closed but not exact, so integrals detect holes — the beginning of topology.
On manifolds one must integrate forms, not functions, because forms carry the Jacobian factor |det| automatically under a change of chart (Satz 4-9).
Green, Divergence and classical Stokes are each obtained by choosing the right form ω of degree 0/1/2; rot grad f = 0 and div rot F = 0 fall out of d²=0 (Problem 4-19b).
methods_math: differential forms and exterior derivative d
wedge product ∧ and alternating/antisymmetric tensors
singular chains and boundary operator ∂
Stokes' theorem (Satz 4-13 and 5-5)
n-dimensional Riemann integration, Lebesgue criterion (measure zero)
Fubini's theorem
change of variables / Jacobian factor |det g'|

Linear map / determinant-as-oriented-area, norm/open-set/boundary classifier, Riemann 2D upper/lower sums, measure-zero covering, Fubini slicing, change-of-variables (all custom 2D canvas)
Partition of unity, alternating-tensor and wedge-product demos, orientation/volume-element, 1-form and 2-form fields, d-operator and d²=0, dθ on ℝ²∖{0} (custom 2D canvas)
Chains and ∂²=0, step-through Stokes proof and a numerical live-verification of ∫dω = ∫_{∂}ω (custom 2D canvas)
Manifold 'locally flat', tangent space in 3D and Möbius band orientability (Plotly 3D surface / custom canvas)
Classical theorems (Green, Divergence in 3D, Stokes) numerically, Archimedes' principle as physics, and a dependency-graph of the book (custom 2D canvas + Plotly)
internal_tensions: The proof is trivial but the 'horde of difficult definitions' is the real content — the page is built to make those definitions tangible.
Whether 'closed ⇒ exact' holds depends on the topology (holes) of the region, not on the formula.
Area defined as a limit of inscribed triangles fails (Schwarz's cylinder); the correct definition is the integral over the volume element.
Partial derivatives alone do not imply differentiability — Satz 2-8 (continuous partials) is only sufficient, not necessary.

title: Vom Weltzugang zum Weltmodell (From World Access to World Model — Coherent Representation)
category_reason: A sheaf-/category-theoretic epistemology of 'world models' that is applied with a dedicated, substantive LLM station (structural necessity of hallucination, model collapse, RLHF as a Tarski anchor) — sheaves/category theory used 'for AI', with a clear AI application.
thesis: A world model is the global section reconstructed from local descent data along an admissible cover — provisional, revisable, and never identical to what it represents; coherence is necessary but not sufficient for truth, and an LLM structurally (not accidentally) confuses the two, which is why it must hallucinate.
key_claims: A world model = a global section glued from locally-compatible sections over an admissible cover (the sheaf/Garben condition: local compatibility ⇒ unique global section).

Coherence (internal consistency) is necessary but NOT sufficient for truth; correspondence ('Kontakt' to W) is a separate, independent test — a self-consistent fantasy passes coherence and fails correspondence.
The class 𝒯 of licensed transformations carries all the content: an unlicensed or overly rich 𝒯 is itself a form of overfitting — more transformation freedom demands more evidence.

The cover never reaches the whole context c, only the accessible interface c_acc ⊆ c; every instrument widens but never closes the cover, so the model is of the interface, not the thing-in-itself (Kant's Ding an sich).

Truth (veridicality) = the limit of (coherence ∧ correspondence) as the W-anchored cover is widened — approximated, never reached, a regulative ideal; justified acceptance = coherence on the current cover ∧ no failed contact point (Popper: not yet falsified), which IS operationalizable.

An LLM is an internal coherence machine without licensed correspondence transitions, so it wins on fitness metrics and structurally must hallucinate; model collapse is predicted because AI-generated corpus text adds only derived patches that do not widen c_acc.

Five pathologies of a model — self-consistent fantasy, fact-book, contact-point liar, calibrated error, question-outside-the-cover — each needs a different cure; the fifth (no contact point at all, the question lies outside c_acc) is the sneakiest and breaks no condition.
Self-application: the framework instantiates 'Pathology 4: calibrated error' — it has a consistent small bias toward presenting a working definition or loose reading with the force of a theorem.

Model-vs-factbook connectivity, Popper risky predictions, pathology simulator, fitness-vs-truth survival sim

internal_tensions: Circularity: the right side of Tarski's T (the fact in the meta-language) is itself a trace, so correspondence secretly becomes coherence at a higher level; the escape is the limit over INDEPENDENT W-anchored widenings (derived patches do not advance it).
c_acc never reaches c — the model is of the interface, not the thing (Kant).

The framework self-identifies as Pathology 4 (calibrated error) and lists three found residues: the Bradley reading (reconstruction, not exegesis), 𝒯 = space of reasons (analogy, not identity), and the Caramello transfer (imprecisely formulated).
The coherence-vs-correspondence four-field: only (coherent ∧ contact) is a good indicator for 'right', and even that is not a proof.

title: Latent Semantic Manifolds in Large Language Models (Mabrok, 2026)
category_reason: A formal information-geometric paper (arXiv:2603.22301) about the geometry of LLM hidden-state representations — Fisher metric, Riemannian semantic manifolds, Voronoi token generation, and rate-distortion bounds, empirically tested on 6 real LLMs.
thesis: Language is a lossy compression of a continuous concept space; contextual hidden states of a transformer lie on a thin Riemannian 'latent semantic manifold' (k≈20 ≪ d) tiled by token Voronoi cells, and there is a provable, unbridgeable loss floor for any finite vocabulary — the first empirical confirmation of a proven geometric theorem about LLM representations.
key_claims: Hypothesis 4.1: for each layer ℓ, contextual hidden states (layer ≥ 1) lie on a smooth compact connected k-dimensional Riemannian submanifold of ℝ^d with k ≈ 15–22 and d = 768–2048, so only 1–3% of the vector space is actually used.
The manifold is GENERATED by the transformer, not inherited from the embedding table — raw token embeddings (layer 0) violate the hypothesis (Robinson et al. 2025; MLE gives a k≈68 artifact there).

Token generation = Voronoi projection: when embeddings have equal norm, argmax ⟨e_t, h⟩ is identical to argmin ‖h − e_t‖ (greedy decoding = nearest-neighbor search); each token's cell volume μ(R_t) measures its conceptual breadth (polysemous vs precise words).

The Fisher metric G = Wᵀ(diag(p) − ppᵀ)W is the canonical metric on hidden states — by Chentsov's theorem it is the only Riemannian metric (up to scale) invariant under sufficient statistics; it is the second derivative of the KL divergence (Prop 12.3).

Satz 10.5 (linear volume law): the normalized expressibility gap η(ε) = [H^{k−1}(∂V)/(λ·vol(M))]·ε + O(ε²) for ε < 1/(2κ_∂); a single scalar α characterizes vocabulary quality; empirically log-log slopes 0.873–1.117 with R² > 0.985 on all 6 models.

Satz 10.8 (fundamental distortion bound): D ≥ c_k·ν_min·(vol(M)/N)^(2/k) — no finite vocabulary reaches zero distortion; halving the loss at k=20 needs ~1024× more tokens, at k=50 ~33 million× (the curse of dimensionality).

There is an 'irreducible ambiguity floor': m_0.05 ≈ 0.04–0.06 across all 6 models despite a 12× parameter range — ~5% of natural-language positions are genuinely ambiguous and no model size removes it (analogous to irreducible loss in scaling laws).

The geometry (k, the hourglass pattern, the linear gap law) is an invariant of the TASK 'next-token prediction on natural language', not of the architecture — identical across GPT-2/OPT/Pythia, 124M–1.5B, different data and tokenizers.

internal_tensions: All evidence is correlation and consistency-checking, not causality — no intervention experiments.
Not tested above 1.5B parameters; if k grows with scale, the rate-distortion / vocabulary-design predictions change fundamentally.
vol(M) is never measured absolutely (only ratios), so Satz 10.8 is qualitative, not numerically verified.
The Fisher metric degenerates when the output distribution becomes sharp (large β, Σ_p → 0) — a stated boundary of the framework.
Layer 0 (raw embeddings) violates the manifold hypothesis, so the hypothesis applies only to contextual states (layer ≥ 1).
Entropy and margin are related but NOT the same (|Spearman ρ| ≈ 0.16–0.23, not ~1); the paper argues margin — not entropy — is the right quantity for 'can language express this thought'.

title: Transformer — geometrisch
category_reason: A minimal interactive 3D animation that explains one transformer block (embeddings, positional encoding, attention, FFN) purely geometrically for a polysemous German sentence — a clear transformer/attention explainer.
thesis: A single transformer block is a purely geometric operation on points in ℝ³ — tokens as points, positional encoding as a fixed rotation, attention as projecting onto a learned query ray and softmaxing those lengths, then moving the query token to the weighted center of mass, followed by a spatial warp (FFN) — repeated six times to disambiguate 'Bank' in 'Die Bank war kalt.'
key_claims: Each word is a point in 3D space; 'Bank' starts exactly halfway between two meaning 'ghost points' (Sitzbank/furniture and Geldhaus/money), i.e. undecided, and context resolves it.
Positional encoding = a fixed rotation per step (72° helix): 'position becomes an angle, not a number.'

Attention = drop a perpendicular (Lot) from each token onto a query 'search ray' (the learned question direction, pointing from 'Bank' toward 'kalt'); the length on the ray is the raw score, longer = better fit.
The lengths become softmax shares a₁+a₂+a₃=1 (longer → bigger share); temperature anneals as the step plays.
The attention output moves the query token to the weighted center of mass of the tokens (new = a₁P₁ + a₂P₂ + a₃P₃, 'like a seesaw').
The FFN is a warp of the whole embedding space (x → f(x)), the second sub-layer of each block, shown as a bent grid.
Stacking six such geometric steps traces a trajectory per word through the layers ('Und das sechsmal hintereinander').
methods_math: token embeddings as points in ℝ³
rotational positional encoding (fixed-angle helix)
attention as projection onto a query direction + softmax over projection lengths
weighted centroid / convex combination (residual update)
FFN as a coordinate warp/diffeomorphism of the space
layer stacking / trajectory per token
visualizations: Single full-screen custom canvas 2D projection of a 3D scene (hand-rolled 3D→2D camera with drag-to-rotate and zoom), animating 7 keyframed 'images' (Bilder 1–7) with eased transitions and a keyboard/progress bar; no external viz or math-rendering library (formulas are HTML/CSS text).
internal_tensions: It is a minimal intuition/preview artifact (7 fixed slides, one hand-crafted sentence and one query token) — a pedagogical reduction, not a full treatment.
It omits multi-head attention, attention masking/softmax masking, layer normalization, and any real learned weights — all geometry is hand-set for the 'Bank/kalt' polysemy example.
It is a variant/companion in the transformer_rein_geometrisch family (v1/v3 in other batches).
